ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, subscribers, officers and UBOs against: (i) FINTRAC's PCMLTFA obligations and FINTRAC Guidance on politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign PEPs, heads of international organizations, and their family members and close associates); (ii) UN Consolidated List and Canadian implementing regulations under the United Nations Act, Special Economic Measures Act, and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law); (iii) the consolidated Canadian sanctions list maintained by Global Affairs Canada and enforced by OSFI-regulated institutions; (iv) OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists, mandated because the target payment rails are USD Swift_TT and Escrow_Inspection_Wire; and (v) trade-control checks including Canada's Export Control List and WTO/anti-dumping orders on semiconductors. Enhanced due diligence is required for the 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced' spot semiconductor trading profile: verification of source of funds, corporate-veil penetration to natural persons, corroboration of beneficial ownership against the ISC register, negative-news monitoring, and senior-management approval for the client relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), administered through the network of licensed Alberta Registry Agents using the Alberta Corporate Registrations system and integrated NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) reporting; identical NUANS reports may also be used for an elective federal Canada Business Corporations Act incorporation filed with Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the ABCA and its regulations, a corporate name may be in English, French, or a bilingual English/French combination, and must include a prescribed legal element (e.g., Inc., Corp., Ltd., Ltd., Ltée). Names using non-official languages or non-Roman scripts must be transliterated into Roman characters and accompanied by an official-language translation in the articles; the NUANS search is conducted against the transliterated form. Numerals and punctuation are permitted subject to distinctiveness and non-confusion standards.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Royal, Crown, Premier, Minister, Government, Parliamentary, Heritage
Co-operative, Coop, Foundation, Association, Chamber of Commerce
Canada, Alberta (in a context implying Crown sponsorship or governmental patronage)
Foreign, International, Export, Import (where implying official status or requiring ministerial consent)
Olympic, RCMP, Police, Board of Trade (protected marks requiring authorizing consent)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Corporate Registry rejects a proposed name or the articles are refused on name grounds, the applicant: (1) may refile corrected articles with a new distinctive element; (2) may, within 30 days of refusal, submit a written reconsideration request to Service Alberta - Corporate Registry attaching the NUANS report and a written legal argument distinguishing the proposed name from conflicting names and trademarks, including consent letters where a conflicting holder is willing to waive; (3) may, for a final administrative refusal, apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review within the applicable limitation period; and (4) may elect to incorporate federally under the CBCA where the Alberta registry outcome remains unsuitable. Third-party objections to a granted name may trigger the Registrar's post-incorporation cancellation or compulsory change proceedings.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. The ABCA requires the corporation to maintain, at all times, a registered office within Alberta at a physical street address (a post office box alone is prohibited) where notices and process may be served during normal business hours, and where corporate records and the ISC register can be produced. For this wholesale SSD/CPU trading entity, with no inventory or employees at the registered office, a regulated virtual office offering a real Alberta street address, mail handling, service-of-process acceptance and records custody is acceptable. However, commercial banks and escrow agents may require a physical operational presence or a notarized place-of-business verification before opening Swift_TT or Escrow_Inspection_Wire facilities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk over the first 24 months for a 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced' wholesale semiconductor broker is approximately 35%; unannounced on-site inspection by Service Alberta Corporate Registry for a non-licensed standard registrant is statistically low (under 10% annually), but the probability rises materially to about 40% where a corporate bank, correspondent bank, or escrow provider commissions a physical business-activity verification of the registered office and trading premises. Mitigation includes a professionally managed registered office, immediate availability of the ISC/UBO register, clean records, and a documented spot-trading compliance file ready for FINTRAC-bank co-inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 7, 10, 12, 18, 104(1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; Articles may authorize common shares without required initial contribution. incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, pursuant to the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), that the incorporators accept and subscribe to the common shares as stated in the Articles, and that the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at the address recorded in the Articles in Calgary, Alberta. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the draft bylaws presented be, and are hereby, adopted as the complete code of corporate governance. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the individuals named in the consent schedule are elected as directors, and the directors appoint Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary of the Corporation, each to hold office until successors are appointed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry System (ACRS) — Name Request Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request through an authorized Alberta corporate registry agent or online portal. Review the report to confirm the corporate name is distinct from existing names and trademarks. Reserve the selected name for 90 days and obtain the Name Search Result document.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a new Name Search Request or submit written consent from the conflicting name holder permitting use of the same or composite name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator or licensed corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 2 Articles of Incorporation specifying corporate name, registered office address (Calgary, Alberta), share classes, directors, and any restrictions on business. Ensure the incorporator signs the Articles and the required Consent to Act as Director forms are executed by each director.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Before filing, amend the Articles or Consent forms; if rejected, re-execute corrected signatures or modify the share structure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Articles and File for Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed Articles via ACRS online, by mail, or in person at an authorized registry agent. Pay the statutory filing fee using credit card or bank transfer. Once processed, the Corporate Registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing contains substantive defects and is refused, correct the Articles and refile; no legal effect occurs until certification. Minor administrative errors may be cured via an Application for Correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation, Corporate Extract and Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, download the Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Extract from ACRS. Register with CRA through Business Registration Online to obtain a nine-digit Business Number (BN) and applicable program accounts (GST/HST, payroll, income tax).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA registration is deferred or problematic, contact the CRA business hotline; amend corporate address or director information via ACRS to avoid mismatch.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, By-law Adoption and Officer Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Call and hold the first directors' meeting, or obtain unanimous written resolutions. Approve the pro-forma first board resolution to ratify share subscriptions, fix the registered office, adopt the bylaws, and appoint officers. Record minutes and keep them in the corporate records book.
required_dossiers: Notice or explanatory record of meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum is not achieved, circulate a written resolution signed by all directors or unanimous incorporator consent to satisfy Business Corporations Act requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) is the competent federal authority for Part I corporate income tax and for GST/HST under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (ETA). The primary registration and filing portals are Business Registration Online (BRO), CRA My Business Account, and the CRA Business Gateway API for third-party filers. Alberta corporate income tax (8% general rate) is administered and collected by the CRA on behalf of Alberta under the federal-provincial Tax Collection Agreement and the Alberta Corporate Tax Act (RSA 2000, c. C-28); the Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA) is the provincial counterpart responsible for non-income tax compliance programs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Alberta Business Corporations Act; appoint a Canadian resident registered office and, if the beneficial owner is foreign, a resident agent for service of process. (2) Apply for the 9-digit Business Number (BN) through Business Registration Online or Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number', selecting the program accounts: RP (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), RM (CBSA import/export), and RC (payroll, if Canadian employees are hired). (3) GST/HST registration is compulsory for any person engaged in a commercial activity in Canada whose worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any four consecutive calendar quarters (ETA s. 148); an export-only wholesaler should nevertheless register voluntarily to recover input tax credits on Canadian warehousing, logistics, and overhead costs. (4) File the T2 Corporate Income Tax Return and the Alberta corporate tax allocation annually through the same BN; GST/HST returns are filed electronically via My Business Account, GST/HST NETFILE, or the Business Gateway API. (5) Maintain the BN program accounts in good standing even in years of nil revenue; CRA imposes late-filing penalties under ITA s. 162 and ETA s. 280 and may suspend refund offsets.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A corporation incorporated in Canada is resident in Canada under common law and section 250 of the Income Tax Act; it is therefore taxable on worldwide income and no pass-through treatment is available. The small business deduction (9% federal plus 2% Alberta on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income) is restricted to Canadian-controlled private corporations and is unavailable where 50% or more of the equity is held by non-residents. Territorial scope is worldwide taxation for resident corporations; a non-resident corporation carrying on business through a permanent establishment in Canada would be taxed only on Canadian-source business income, but that model does not apply to the Canadian-incorporated subsidiary contemplated here. No tax-exempt zone exists in Alberta.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box classification regime. The relevant statutory elections are: (a) ITA s. 85 rollover election (Forms T2057/T2058) to incorporate contributed property at tax-deferred agreed amounts; (b) ITA s. 249.1 election to adopt a non-calendar taxation year; (c) ministerial discretion under ITA s. 256(9) regarding associated-corporation determinations; (d) ETA s. 156 election for closely related corporations to deem intercorporate supplies to be made for nil consideration; (e) ETA s. 180(1) election permitting a non-resident to appoint a resident accredited agent, making agent and principal jointly and severally liable for GST/HST - relevant for foreign-owned intra-group brokerage structures; (f) hybrid-mismatch outcomes are addressed automatically by ITA ss. 18.4, 18.5, 20.2 (effective for years beginning on or after July 1, 2022) with no protective election available to override them; (g) the GST/HST quick-method election is available only to resident small suppliers and is generally disadvantageous for zero-rated exporters.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) with supervision by Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and AML/ATF regulation by FINTRAC
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully free-floating currency regime with unrestricted current and capital account convertibility. The Canadian Dollar (CAD) is freely convertible without exchange controls. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and capital repatriation may proceed without foreign-exchange administration approval, subject to corporate solvency tests under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) and applicable Canadian withholding tax on payments to non-residents (typically 25% statutory rate, subject to tax treaty reduction). Eligibility to obtain treaty benefits requires tax-residence certificates, and CA-AB corporate residency must be substantiated with Canadian board meetings, major supplier decisions, and inventory sourcing protocols. Cross-border wire transfers and large-cash transactions above CAD 10,000 are reportable to FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA. Funds originating from, or destined to, sanctioned jurisdictions are prohibited under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act. No central-bank approval is required for converting export receipts or making foreign currency payments; however, Schedule I banks may apply their own compliance overlays on OFAC-listed or high-risk counterparties
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation, or conversion requirements on export proceeds. There is no mandated timeline to bring export receipts into Canada, nor any mandatory conversion of foreign currency export earnings into CAD. Exporters may retain funds in foreign currency accounts with Canadian authorized banks. Nevertheless, the PCMLTFA requires that records of all export/import payments and associated wire transfers be retained for at least five years. Exporters must also report suspicious transactions and large cash or virtual-currency transactions to FINTRAC. The bank's internal AML policies may require proof of shipment within a reasonable commercial period to avoid trade-based money-laundering red flags, particularly in the spot semiconductor wholesale sector. To mitigate, the CA_AB treasury function should maintain fully reconciled digital ledgers of export trade documents and wire histories per transaction

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational CAD/USD Account with Escrow Wire Solutions
Cross-Border Multi-Currency Account and Trade Finance Account
Operational Account for Alberta-Based Wholesale Entity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility with strict legal constraints. Non-resident Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) cannot provide electronic money services or payment accounts to Canadian residents unless registered as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and, where applicable, authorized under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) with Bank of Canada oversight. Unregistered offshore EMIs holding Canadian client funds are non-compliant and expose the entity to bank de-risking. Wise, Payoneer, and Airwallex may be used under a Canadian-partnered regulated model, but must not serve as the primary treasury custody or settlement layer. The recommended architecture uses a Schedule I bank as the primary clearing account, while regulated FINTRAC-registered payment service providers facilitate low-value vendor payouts and expense disbursements. A compliance package must include the EMI's FINTRAC MSB registration number, RPAA authorization or exemption, and contractual confirmation that funds are held in segregated settlement accounts at a Canadian or equivalent regulated financial institution
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is generally available for Canadian Business Corporations at Schedule I banks, but the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML classification in the semiconductor wholesale sector may trigger an enhanced due-diligence stream requiring a live video interview with at least one director or authorized signatory. Full physical appearance is not a statutory requirement under federal banking regulation, but banks may require in-person identity verification for non-resident controlling parties or complex beneficial-ownership structures. Where the entity is incorporated federally and extra-provincially registered in Alberta, the bank may require a Canadian director or a registered agent with a physical Alberta address to satisfy 'nexus' expectations. Defense dossier: certified true copies of Articles of Incorporation and Alberta extra-provincial registration, registered office address, director and officer register, UBO attestation, board resolutions authorizing account opening, and a completed business-profile questionnaire describing the SSD/CPU wholesale business model, expected counterparties, jurisdictions, and transaction volumes

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs or corporate shareholders registered in tax-avoidance or offshore jurisdictions causing enhanced scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO declaration and corporate group organogram; certified passport copies of all natural-person beneficial owners; source-of-wealth statement and non-resident shareholder due-diligence file; certificates of good standing from home jurisdiction; evidence of economic substance in Canada; bank-specific UBO attestation form

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering risk arising from same-day or high-volume buy/sell of SSD and CPU processors with tight margins
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders and vendor invoices; air waybills, bills of lading, and Canada Border Services Agency cargo reports; warehouse inventory movement records; HS-commodity tariff codes and product serial numbers; independent pricing sources or quotation sheets providing arm's-length price verification; complete audit trail for each wire and goods movement

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Round-tripping or inter-company back-to-back payment flows through related Canadian entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany agreements with commercial substance; board resolutions approving related-party treasury transactions; transfer-pricing documentation under section 247 of the Income Tax Act, including OECD-compliant master file and local file if thresholds are met; cash-flow forecast and commercial justification for the flow; reconciliation of goods flow to payment flow

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually large inbound wires from escrow or foreign counterparties before goods title transfers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow or inspection-based sales contract with payment-release milestones; counterparty onboarding KYC file and source-of-funds evidence; bank reference from the sending institution; escrow agent's verification of the goods milestone; exception-log description of the commercial rationale; FINTRAC large-transaction reporting if over CAD 10,000

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparty or sanctioned jurisdiction involvement in the supply chain (e.g., addresses in OFAC or Canada-sanctioned countries)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time sanctions screening policy and system logs; legal opinion on permissible dealings and supply-chain licensing; confirmation from counterparty that goods are not of sanctioned origin; end-user certificate or re-export risk assessment; refusal-of-transaction register; board AML/ATF policy and annual training records

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection from non-resident shareholders should be routed via SWIFT MT103 to the CA_AB Operational Account, with payment field 70 (Remittance Information) indicating 'Capital Injection / Paid-in Capital' and the corporate file number. The director's resolution approving the issuance of shares must pre-date the wire. Purpose code conventions following the IMF Balance of Payments classification: use the 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital' category, and alert the bank relationship manager in advance. FINTRAC reporting is required for the transaction if CAD-equivalent exceeds 10,000. The bank will require evidence of the shareholder's source of funds, beneficial ownership, and corporate solvency. To avoid inadvertent debt characterization, deposit the funds into a dedicated Capital Escrow Account first and issue shares only after KYC clearance and funds received. For a CBCA business corporation extra-provincially registered in Alberta, capital duty and stamp duty do not apply; the shareholder register and CBCA annual return must be updated within the applicable filing window
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 payment transfers for supplier prepayments, verified distributor settlements, and payment against invoice where goods are already shipped or in bonded transit; (2) Documentary Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) issued by a Canadian Schedule I bank for large non-schedule vendor settlements, especially for high-value CPU and SSD purchases, with Incoterms and inspection certificate triggers; (3) Escrow release transfers tied to inspection certification and third-party confirmation; (4) FINTRAC-registered MSB payment rails for low-value disbursements under CAD 5,000, capped by policy to avoid becoming a primary clearing mechanism. All outbound disbursements must be matched against a signed purchase order, vendor invoice, packing list, and logistics documents. Payment/consulting fees and royalties from non-resident suppliers must be separately classified to apply Canadian withholding tax where required under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act. Maintain a complete SWIFT reference and purpose-code log for each outbound payment to satisfy the bank's trade-based AML checks
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD, CNY/CAD) with a Canadian Schedule I bank or FINTRAC-registered derivatives dealer
Cross-currency swap (USD/CAD) for hedging long-term intercompany capital or liquidity mismatches
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on emerging-market currencies (e.g., INR, KRW, IDR) to hedge synthetic exposure where delivery restrictions exist, documented under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
Plain-vanilla FX options (call/put USD/CAD) purchased from a regulated Canadian or OECD dealer, limited to hedge-only product mandates
FX swap (swap of principal/interest in two currencies) to fund short-term CAD liquidity needs and rebalance USD trade proceeds
Rolling spot-deferred contracts offered by regulated FX providers, provided they align with hedge accounting and do not introduce leveraged or exotic features

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation, amalgamation, or extra-provincial registration in Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 late-filing surcharge; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to dissolve the corporation under ABCA s. 216.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (mandatory only if incorporated under the CBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation or continuance under the CBCA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Two consecutive years of non-filing triggers a notice of intent to dissolve under CBCA s. 263(5); administrative dissolution follows if returns remain unfiled.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal return with Alberta corporate income tax schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for the federal Crown and Alberta Treasury Board and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the 6th month after fiscal year-end (e.g., a December 31 year-end is due June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax balance, plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; repeat offenders face 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months; minimum CAD 100 penalty where no tax is owing; daily compound interest applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Return (annual, quarterly, or monthly depending on revenue)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly and quarterly filers: within 1 month after each reporting period; annual filers (gross revenues at or below CAD 1.5 million): within 3 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 1% of net tax owing plus 25% of related interest; increased to 2% plus 50% of interest for repeat failures within a 3-year period; daily compound interest on unpaid amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T106 Information Return (non-arm's length cross-border transactions)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; required where aggregate consideration for non-arm's length transactions with non-residents exceeds CAD 1 million
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 per month per affected non-resident, up to CAD 2,500 per failure; gross negligence penalties up to CAD 24,000 for knowingly false or incomplete filings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Private Alberta corporations are exempt from a mandatory statutory audit; the auditor may be waived by a unanimous shareholder resolution renewed annually. A compulsory audit is triggered if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares demand an audit, the corporation becomes a reporting issuer, or a lender, regulator, or parent-company covenant requires audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook Part I (IFRS) for publicly accountable enterprises; Part II (ASPE / Canadian GAAP) for private corporations; a foreign parent consolidating under IFRS may impose IFRS at the Canadian entity level.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under ABCA s. 114.1 (and CBCA s. 21.1 if federally incorporated), the corporation must maintain an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register identifying any person directly or indirectly holding 25% or more of voting shares or exercising de facto control; the register must be updated within 15 days of any share transfer or control change and kept at the registered office. There is no separate annual UBO filing to the Alberta registry for private corporations; annual statutory confirmation is effected through the Alberta Annual Return, which attests to the registered office and director roster.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250-700 per year (CAD 350-950 typical Alberta registered office and corporate agent retainer)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000-25,000 for a full statutory audit; USD 4,000-10,000 for a review engagement when the audit is waived

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Combined headline rate is 23%, comprising the 15% federal general corporate rate after the 13% general rate reduction and the 8% Alberta general corporate rate. No general statutory tax holiday exists at the federal or Alberta level. Applicable incentives are deductions and credits, not tax holidays: federal SR&ED investment tax credit at 15% for non-CCPCs and 35% for CCPCs on qualifying expenditures; accelerated capital cost allowance for manufacturing and processing equipment; and the Alberta small business corporate tax rate of 2% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, available only to Canadian-controlled private corporations and therefore not available to a non-resident-controlled wholesale broker.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed through CRA Corporation Internet Filing via My Business Account or commercial tax preparation software. Electronic filing is mandatory for corporations with gross revenue exceeding CAD 1,000,000. Alberta corporate income tax is collected by the CRA under the federal-provincial taxation collection agreement, so there is no separate Alberta corporate income tax return filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed within six months after the corporation's fiscal period-end. The balance of tax due is payable within two months after the fiscal period-end, or within three months for a CCPC eligible for the small business deduction in the relevant taxation year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporation identification: legal name, Canadian Business Number (BN), fiscal period-end, country of incorporation, Alberta permanent establishment address and operating business activity classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark the non-resident corporation designation; use the Alberta permanent establishment address as the Canadian service address; do not list the foreign head office as the Canadian address unless that office is also the actual place of Canadian business management.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue: gross wholesale proceeds from SSD and CPU chip sales, including volume rebates and commissions, net of returns, allowances and customer discounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue attributable to the Alberta permanent establishment under the arm's-length allocation rules. Do not include principal-to-principal offshore sales in which the Canadian entity has no participation or risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: opening inventory plus semiconductor purchases, freight-in, import duties and inspection costs less closing inventory. LIFO is not accepted for Canadian tax purposes; use FIFO, average cost or specific item valuation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the arm's-length intercompany price for chips bought from a non-resident affiliate. Ensure Incoterms are accurately documented; freight or inspection costs billed to customers may be reportable as part of gross revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit: Box 020 minus Box 030; used as the starting point for operating expense reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident corporations, gross profit must be connected with the Canadian business. Gross margin should be consistent with the wholesale distribution functional profile.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: salaries, rent, logistics, shipping, escrow-service fees, professional fees, marketing, depreciation and other deductible outlays.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses wholly applicable to the Canadian permanent establishment. Payments to the foreign head office or related service company are deductible only if supported by real services rendered and priced at arm's length; head-office management allocation alone is not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable capital gains and allowable capital losses: 50% inclusion rate of capital gains and 50% deductible amount of allowable capital losses from disposal of capital property.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident disposing of taxable Canadian property must comply with section 116, file Form T2062 and obtain a clearance certificate before the proceeds are paid to the vendor; inventory of SSD/CPU chips is not generally taxable Canadian property if sold in the ordinary course of the Canadian wholesale business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before loss carryovers: gross profit minus operating expenses, adjusted for capital gains/losses, dividends from taxable Canadian corporations and other adjustments in the T2 taxability schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may deduct only losses connected with the Canadian permanent establishment. Foreign losses cannot reduce Canadian-source taxable income; the amount must be computed using the same accounting principles as the T2 financial statement basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: net income before carryovers reduced by eligible non-capital loss carryforwards, restricted farm losses and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Canadian-source non-capital losses carried forward up to 20 years or carried back three years. The loss claim must be made against the Canadian permanent establishment's income only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Part I federal tax payable: taxable income multiplied by the 15% general federal corporate rate, with any applicable foreign tax credits and investment tax credits claimed on the corresponding schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation, federal abatement is calculated on income allocated to the Canadian permanent establishment; the 15% rate is the net general rate after the 10% provincial abatement and 13% general rate reduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial tax payable: Alberta taxable income allocated to Alberta using T2 Schedule 5, multiplied by the 8% Alberta general corporate rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the corporate group has permanent establishments in more than one province, allocate taxable income using the statutory gross revenue and payroll formula; for a non-resident corporation with only an Alberta PE, all Canadian taxable income is allocated to Alberta.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under ITA subsection 162(2) is 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% for each full month of delay, up to a maximum of 17%. Prescribed interest accrues daily on all unpaid federal and Alberta tax. Knowingly filing false statements attracts the subsection 163(2) gross negligence penalty of 50% of the tax sought to be evaded, and criminal prosecution under subsection 239(1) can result in fines of 50% to 200% of the evaded amount and imprisonment of up to 5 years.
